newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isuzu studying European engine output.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu studying European engine output.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd is studying the feasibility of producing diesel engines in Europe, an Isuzu spokesman said on Wednesday.
"But we have not decided on any details yet, such as production volume, the plant site and investment cost. Poland is one of the candidate countries," the spokesman said.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a Japanese economic daily, reported on Saturday that Isuzu would invest 50 billion yen to produce diesel engines in Poland at an annual rate of 300,000 units.

Industry sources said the feasibility study covers a plan by Isuzu to produce 1,500cc and 1,700cc engines for Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp (GM). Adam Opel is planning to set up a unit in Poland to produce cars.
Isuzu, owned 37.4 percent by General Motors, supplied 186,000 Japanese-made diesel engines to Opel in 1995.

In eastern Europe, Magyar Suzuki Corp of Hungary, owned 40 percent by Suzuki Motor Corp, produced Cultus compact cars at a rate of 42,000 units in the year to March 1996. It plans to produce 50,000 in 1996/97.
